publicText: Civic Hall announced a New York City Council hackathon focused on constituent services for January 30, 2016, from 1-3 p.m.

evidence.note: Directly supports the announced date, time, Council relationship, and constituent-services purpose.
Preserves the embedded Civic Hall post; it is not a dedicated event listing.

caveat: The 1-3 p.m. period is the announced event time. A participant photograph timestamp of approximately 2:10 p.m. is separate evidence.
antiClaims: The Wayback capture is the event's Civic Hall calendar listing.
The participant photograph time is the event start time.

publicText: An event-day New York City Council post identified the gathering at Civic Hall as its first CouncilStat hackathon.

evidence.note: Preserves the Council post through Civic Hall's embedded social feed.

publicText: The promotional graphic attached to Civic Hall's post used the branding 'New York City Council Hackathon' and displayed labs.council.nyc.

evidence.note: The wording and labs.council.nyc reference are visible in the graphic.

caveat: Treat this as recovered event branding, not proof of a longer formal registration title.

publicText: After the full CouncilStat dataset was released, Jamie independently developed CallNYC.org as a resident-facing interpretation of the records.

evidence.note: The article reports that Jamie encountered the data at the Civic Hall event and created CallNYC after the full dataset was released.
Public code repository documents the independent project artifact.

caveat: CallNYC was not an official Council product and is now an archived, unofficial prototype.
antiClaims: Jamie built CallNYC during the hackathon.
CallNYC was an official New York City Council product.
CallNYC was a formal hackathon submission.

publicText: Council staff cautioned that district offices used CouncilStat differently and with different frequency, so case counts could not responsibly be treated as a standardized measure of office performance.

evidence.note: The article reports the Council's caution about differing office usage and frequency.

antiClaims: Higher CouncilStat counts measured better service.
The dataset was complete or consistently entered across offices.

publicText: Jamie participated in the Council's first CouncilStat hackathon at Civic Hall in January 2016, then independently built CallNYC after the full dataset release.

evidence.note: Supports the CouncilStat hackathon and Civic Hall setting.
Supports Jamie's participation and the independent follow-on project after release.

caveat: CallNYC was not built during the hackathon and was not an official Council product.
